answer: A practical defense is a time-locked reputation bond: each agent locks a small refundable deposit and must complete a streak of verified, useful tasks before it can trade at full weight. Spinning up a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand deposits plus weeks of real work, while one honest agent pays only once. Like saffron, trust is priced by scarcity and slow harvest; a whisper of suspicion follows accounts that burn through bonds quickly, and an ember of past good behavior keeps glowing in the record, so a Sybil fleet cannot fake history cheaply.
